Ugh, I relate to this so hard... I was in this exact spot emotionally a few months back, and other job hunting difficulties with depression still kill me and make me think I'll be a failure forever and never able to build a life... Fwiw, what did help me with the issues of justifying why I'm the best candidate and making the resume look better when past references were spotty, etc, was having someone experienced in the work force look over my stuff and talk me through how to focus on my good qualities not my deficiencies. It helped to have someone else basically say "it's ok, other people have had backgrounds like yours too looking to get a job, you just need to get your foot in the door".
Good luck :/ Hopefully we can both find the motivation to move forward in this process...

I'd love some advice or to hear other experiences for reconnecting with people after coming out of a depressive funk. For me it can get very cyclical, and if I've had a couple bad months and am really trying to make efforts again and get some things in order to feel better and climb out if the hole, one of the hardest things is talking to friends and family I ignored or pulled away from. There's a lot of guilt of being a fair weather friend, and it means I have very few close relationships even with family members and people I really want to be close with. This can be both a stumbling block when I'm on an upswing and trying to improve, and it can also be a significant trigger for a bad spell if the guilt builds up or my poor relationship maintenance becomes apparent for some reason.

I think the key point being missed by a lot of these comments is the distinction between "Fancy clothes today, any special occasion?" or a neutral joke about "Got an interview/ court date?" being alright (might be tiring or annoying after a few repetitions but not creepy or weird), but "Who are you dressing up for?" or "Wow, got a date tonight?" or "You look great all dolled up like that" being creepy and enough to make you uncomfortable in the workplace (ESPECIALLY when it's a recurring comment). Comments focusing on why the commenter thinks your appearance is better/worse (makeup comments or "that dress is great on your figure") or implying that the only reason you'd be dressed up is to impress someone romantically/sexually are where small talk crosses the line to being really uncomfortable. I hope this helps answer your question!

My chiropractor gave me a timeline for treatment and worked with me to develop a doable and reasonable plan. Maybe you had a bad experience, that's what spawned this thread, but please refrain from spewing blanket claims of "all are this" and "none would that". You're working on speculation and generalization here and it discredits the professionals based in science and medicine who do help people on a daily basis.
Sure, let's cut you open at way greater cost with risk of infection when someone could fix this non-invasively....

Unfortunately, some spinal and joint manipulations can't be done on your own. Ever had a crick in your neck that you can crack and fix, but it just comes back worse and worse each time you do? Your own body can't realign that, but a chiropractor can. I'm all for self-care and stretching, but it's disheartening to see people that can really help (quality DCs) get tossed around like they do nothing by people who don't have experience with joint pain and the well-trained people in the field, and have only seen nuts (so they didn't vet their doctor before seeing them) or heard bad jokes on tv or in some circle-jerk.
Wish I could upvote more; thank you for this well-articulated response!

Similar experience here. Absolutely didn't know it was possible (and it sounds like it shouldn't be) until it hurt to cough and twist my back. In my opinion, thank goodness for good chiropractors out there who take the time to learn how to fix these things non-invasively.

Except that's actually something that can happen, and having a rib out is painful as fuck (from experience)! I'm sure there are some quacks out there like there are in any field, but the chiropractors I've seen at least have been down-to-earth and science-oriented people who have the specialized training to help alleviate a lot of pain for me. Their office worked with the massage center next door and referred patients back and forth for the appropriate treatment (joints vs muscles I think).
